props.title: Duel
props.initialSlug: An epic battle of man vs. machine.

sections.content: **Duel** (1971) announced Steven Spielberg's arrival as a master of sustained tension. This made-for-TV thriller follows a business commuter terrorized by a menacing truck driver on remote California highways. At just 24, Spielberg turned a simple premise into 90 minutes of pure automotive anxiety, using innovative camera angles and minimal dialogue. The film directly influenced countless vehicle-based thrillers like **The Hitcher** (1986) and **Joy Ride** (2001), while establishing Spielberg's trademark technique of withholding the villain's face to build mystery.

sections.content: The success of **Duel** spawned an entire subgenre of highway horror films. **Race with the Devil** (1975) added occult elements, while **The Car** (1977) went supernatural. These road-based thrillers peaked in the 1990s with intelligent entries like **Breakdown** (1997) and **Roadkill** (1989). Each film built on Spielberg's core insight - that highways represent both freedom and vulnerability, where help can be miles away.

The film's influence extends beyond obvious vehicle-chase movies. Its DNA appears in slasher films like **The Hitcher** (1986), where the open road becomes a trap. Even modern tech thrillers like **Cellular** (2004) echo **Duel's** premise of an everyday person pursued by an unseen tormentor. The film's economical storytelling and mounting dread influenced horror classics like **Halloween** (1978), proving less dialogue often equals more suspense. sections.content: Spielberg's camera techniques in **Duel** revolutionized action filming. He mounted cameras on car hoods and truck grilles, creating visceral point-of-view shots that became standard in chase sequences. These innovations influenced films like **The French Connection** (1971) and **Mad Max** (1979). The director's use of the massive Peterbilt truck as a character itself - never fully revealed, always menacing - established a template for mechanical antagonists, from **Christine** (1983) to **Maximum Overdrive** (1986).
